FAST

NEW DELHI: Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the "Cockroach" youth movement in Delhi on Saturday ( Oct 10) as security forces locked down parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India's election chief. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended in the central business district and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a demonstration organised by the Cockroach movement. The protest was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The movement had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, but the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began.

A home ministry official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters more than 2,000 people were detained in Delhi. Local media said about 400 protesters were held in India's financial hub, Mumbai. There was no immediate comment from police on the detentions. The United Nations human rights office expressed concerns over mass detentions before and during the protests. "We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled," UN Human Rights Spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan said in a statement. He also urged authorities to engage in "meaningful dialogue" to address the "broadly held" concerns expressed. The Indian mission to the UN in Geneva, however, called the UN's concerns "misplaced" and said they constitute "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India." It stressed that the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by India's Constitution. "As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order," the statement added.

Watch:

New Delhi under lockdown as police clamp down on protests, detain Cockroach Party founder

MOVEMENT LEADERS HELD Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka when their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi, the group said in a statement. Television footage showed Dipke challenging officers who approached him on board the aircraft. "I have come to be arrested, arrest me ... I am not afraid of you guys," he said. "No, this is not an arrest," one officer replied. "Please cooperate." The movement condemned what it called the "authoritarian detention" of its leaders, demanded their release and vowed to continue protesting. "We will continue our protest tomorrow, day after ... until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. We will be on the streets," CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde told reporters. CJP also said authorities refused to provide updates on the leaders' whereabouts or health, even after news arrived of the death of Dipke's grandmother. Police said Dipke was informed of her death and was offered help to return home for the funeral.

Read more:

CNA Explains: What India’s ‘cockroach’ protests reveal about a generation under pressure

Some opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee of West Bengal, Arvind Kejriwal of Delhi, and Pinarayi Vijayan of Kerala were also detained, TV channels showed. Representatives of two digital news outlets said police briefly detained four of their reporters while they were covering the demonstrations. A Reuters journalist was also detained briefly before being released. Across the capital of about 20 million people, security forces set up checkpoints on major roads and entry points, boarded buses searching for protesters and inspected vehicles. Barricades and concrete blocks disrupted traffic while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear-gas launchers guarded key routes.

Related:

Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder ahead of youth protest

NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The demonstrations represent one of the most serious tests yet for Modi, stemming from allegations that election authorities improperly revised voter rolls ahead of recent state polls . Protests intensified after the Indian Express reported last week that two election commissioners had questioned Kumar's voter-list revisions that removed roughly 130 million names from voter lists. Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied allegations of wrongdoing. The BJP says its electoral success reflects Modi's popularity and India's economic growth, and accuses opposition parties of spreading misinformation. The near daily protests come just months after demonstrations over exam paper leaks forced his education minister to quit . The unrest also comes ahead of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027. Rahul Gandhi, leader of the main opposition Congress party, said Modi's opponents would not back down. A senior BJP member, Ravi Shankar Prasad, said the party was not opposed to demonstrations but the street protests had been "weaponised" by rivals due to election defeats.

Related:

Hundreds from India's Gen Z-led 'cockroach' party protest, seek election chief's resignation

DELETIONS AFFECTED STATE POLLS, OPPOSITION ALLEGES Opposition parties say the deletions affected the outcome of recent state elections won by the BJP and have cast a shadow over voting in the world's largest democracy. Election Commission data show about 130 million voter entries were removed during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated, 30 million who could not be traced and 28 million who had died. The commission says the removals relate to entries identified during the draft revision process and that any eligible voter incorrectly deleted can re-enrol.

Source: Reuters/fs

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 10 : While Tottenham Hotspur have plenty to rue amid a difficult opening to the season, manager Roberto De Zerbi saw something at Old Trafford on Saturday that gave him reason to believe his struggling side may finally be turning a corner. Spurs are 18th and without a victory after six Premier League games following Saturday's 1-1 draw at Manchester United, yet De Zerbi was heartened by the fight his team showed to thoroughly dominate the game and then snatch a stoppage-time equaliser through Dominic Solanke despite being reduced to 10 men. "I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character," De Zerbi told Sky Sports. Bryan Mbeumo scored against the run of play before Tottenham's Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for head-butting Luke Shaw, leaving United fans daring to dream of a much-needed victory, only for Solanke's 92nd-minute header to puncture the mood at Old Trafford.

"We suffered in the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can," De Zerbi said. Rather than fold, Tottenham fought until Solanke headed the equaliser in stoppage time, giving De Zerbi's side more to celebrate than their hosts despite their lowly league position. Spurs, who spent more than £300 million ($397 million) in the transfer market during the close season, have failed to win any of their opening six league matches for only the fourth time in the club's history. Their manager, however, believes there were signs against United that his ideas are beginning to take hold. "We have to believe in ourselves and this football way," De Zerbi said. "If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don't play as a team, it is impossible." For United, there was less cause for optimism. Michael Carrick's side have collected only six points from their first six games, their poorest start to a league campaign since 1986-87, when they had four at the same stage. United struggled desperately before taking the lead through Mbeumo. But even with a man advantage, they failed to put away a Tottenham team that had started the day bottom of the table. "We were mixed (in performance)," Carrick said. "We found it tough first half, it was a challenging first half for us and you could see it just wasn't quite there, it wasn't clicking." The Reds are also winless in the last three league matches when their opponent has had a red card. Carrick was particularly frustrated at allowing Tottenham back into the game that appeared to be United's for the taking. "It's a game we should kill off. And we didn't," he said. "Very disappointed to be in a position like that and not come away with the game." ($1 = 0.7558 pounds)

Source: Reuters

Oct 10 : Nvidia is in talks to deepen its investment in open-source startup Reflection AI or acquire it, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter. • Talks are at an early stage and a deal could take several forms, including a so-called acqui-hire arrangement where Nvidia would hire staff and license technology rather than pursue a full acquisition, potentially avoiding a lengthy regulatory review, the newspaper said. • An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, according to the report, which cited multiple people familiar with the matter, while adding that the discussions could still fall apart. • Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nvidia and Reflection did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside of regular business hours.

FAST

Oct 10 : Barcelona extended their perfect start to the LaLiga season with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Getafe on Saturday, making it eight wins from eight matches and maintaining their lead at the top of the table. The three-week international break did little to disrupt Barcelona’s rhythm and they went ahead after two minutes when Anthony Gordon cut inside and saw his shot deflect off Mario Martin and beyond goalkeeper David Soria. Getafe struggled to escape their own half under sustained pressure and Gabriel Jesus punished a giveaway by Zaid Romero to score on his first start for Barcelona. The hosts remained firmly in control after the break, with Getafe testing Joan Garcia only once on the goalkeeper’s return from injury. Jules Kounde, who had missed a clear chance in the first half, completed the scoring in the 73rd minute with a simple finish from Lamine Yamal’s curling cross. Barcelona lead the standings with 24 points, five ahead of Atletico Madrid and nine clear of Real Madrid, who host Villarreal later on Saturday.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 10 : Manchester United fans revived one of English football's most famous banners on Saturday to taunt Manchester City amid their rival's battle with the Premier League over more than 100 alleged breaches of financial rules. A banner bearing the words "51 YEARS" was unfurled in the Stretford End during United's Premier League game against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. By displaying the figure, United supporters sought to suggest that any trophies won by City between 2009 and 2018 - which form the core of the Premier League's case against the club - should not count, effectively extending their wait for silverware back to their 1976 League Cup success. The banner echoed the "24 YEARS" sign first displayed by United fans in 2000, highlighting City's then two-decade-plus trophy drought.

The banner disappeared after City lifted the FA Cup in 2011, their first major trophy since 1976, before they went on to win multiple Premier League titles, domestic cups and the Champions League. City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 with more than 100 alleged breaches of financial regulations covering a period from 2009 to 2018. Enzo Maresca's team travel to Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since being found guilty of serious breaches of the league's financial rules. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal against the independent commission's verdict.

ZAPORIZHZHIA, Ukraine: Twenty people, including three children, were killed in a Russian attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia on Satur day (Oct 10) , a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a major setback for Kyiv . "To day , Russia said thank you for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, in some of his sharpest criticism yet of the White House. Zaporizhzhia has been a regular target of Russian bombardment with strikes intensifying in the past few months. A 6-year-old girl was among those killed when one strike reduced part of an apartment block to rubble. Her grandfather, Anatoliy Chumniy, stood sobbing over her body, laid on the ground in a white bag, after rescuers pulled it from the wreckage.

"Her birth day would have been at the end of the month," he said through tears. Eighteen others were wounded in the attack on the industrial city , with a pre-war population of over 700,000 and whose outskirts lie less than 30 km (20 miles) from the front line.

Rescuers evacuate wounded residents, Yana and her husband Anton, found under debris of an apartment building damaged during a Russian air strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine October 10, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer

A woman reacts after pulling her relatives from the rubble of a residential building destroyed by a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Kateryna Klochko)

RUSSIA ESCALATING ATTACK S ON UKRAINIAN CITIES It was the third mass-casualty attack on Ukraine this week. Nearly 80 civilians were killed in Russian strikes on Wednes day and Thurs day , including at least 30 killed by a bomb in the eastern garrison city of Kramatorsk and 22 others by a missile in the town of Pryluky, 80 miles east of Kyiv. A senior official in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, said Russia had hit several locations simultaneously in the early hours of Satur day . Rescuers clambered through crumbled masonry to pull other residents of the building out alive. One man, whose leg was trapped in the rubble, screamed in pain as he was being freed. "If (the Russian s) have money, they’ll be able to carry on fighting us," said Nataliia Malysheva, a 49-year-old local resident whose parents died in hospital after being pulled from the rubble. "How many lives have been lost here, how many homes have been destroyed? How many innocent people have died in the meantime?"

Related:

Russian strike on buses kills 30 in frontline Ukrainian city

MOSCOW NEEDS 'DIFFERENT SIGNALS' "Last night provided yet more confirmation that Russia perceives any easing of pressure as a signal that it can supposedly keep fighting, that it can supposedly keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed," Zelenskyy said. A missile attack on Satur day after noon also hit a restaurant, wounding seven people in Kyiv. Russian drones flew over Kyiv throughout the day , part of a vast new wave of bombardment of the capital, the heaviest since the early day s of the war. Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Satur day its drones had struck a data-processing centre in Kyiv and a cargo ship carrying military supplies to the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

Read more:

Commentary: Russia’s new jet‑powered drones mark latest evolution in air war above Ukraine

TRUMP LIFTS DIESEL SANCTIONS Trump 's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports comes as his administration seeks to curb fuel prices, which have risen sharply during the US conflict with Iran. Kyiv had instead urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow in an effort to force it into serious negotiations to end the four-and-a-half-year war. Trump , meanwhile, has criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, which he claims have driven up global prices. Kyiv has said it wants a total halt on all energy strikes by both sides as Moscow pummels Ukraine's power grid. On Satur day , parts of Kyiv and the surrounding region were left without power, bringing the city 's metro trains to a complete halt for the second time this week. The latest strikes came after Ukrainian and European officials held talks with US negotiators in Miami on Fri day aimed at developing a common proposal for ending the war, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Related:

Trump says Putin agrees to major release of diesel to US, global markets

Trump announced the diesel deal while the negotiations were underway, a move Zelenskiy said had caught Kyiv by surprise. The Ukrainian delegation was headed home on Satur day , presidential aide Dmytro Lytvyn was cited by the Interfax Ukraine news agency as saying. Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Trump that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attack s on Moscow . US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Moscow within the next two weeks, Russian state news agency TASS reported on Satur day , citing a source. Four civilians were killed and five others were wounded as a result of Ukrainian attack s on the Russian -controlled Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine, the Russian -installed governor said on Satur day . Reuters could not independently verify the report and there was no immediate comment from Ukraine.

Source: Reuters/fs

LONDON, Oct 10 : Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has had to wait until October to see what his side can do with midfielder Moises Caicedo properly back in the team and he was delighted with his role in the 5-1 demolition of Bournemouth in the Premier League on Saturday. Alonso – who oversaw two victories in his first two matches in charge of Chelsea before failing to win any of the next three - gave Caicedo his first start of the season after being sidelined with a calf problem. The Ecuadorian, 24, provided a stronger shield for Chelsea's defence that has looked shaky since the campaign began and he formed an effective partnership with 36 year-old Jordan Henderson who scored twice. Alonso stressed the importance of Caicedo's return after a brief appearance in August when he lasted only 14 minutes as a substitute before having to limp off.

"With him we have a better midfield area and when you are better in the middle you have a more complete team and something to build around," the Spaniard told reporters. "I am so happy that Moi is feeling better because he is going to be a key player for us. We knew that and we have seen (it) today." In further encouragement for Chelsea fans, right back Marco Palestra - who signed from Atalanta in Italy in the close season but was injured soon after - made his debut as a substitute. The two goals from Henderson and another two from Joao Pedro – both players who have also been in the medical room – and a Morgan Rogers strike underscored Chelsea’s reputation as one of the Premier League’s entertainers this season. They added to their tally of early goals as they rushed into a 2-0 lead within 149 seconds and got their third a little more than 30 seconds after the start of the second half. Cole Palmer celebrated signing a contract extension by providing two assists, adding to the signs that he is getting back to top form.  The only worries for Alonso were Chelsea's failure to keep a clean sheet for a 22nd Premier League game in a row when Bournemouth striker Evanilson briefly gave the visitors hope in the second half, and the absence of captain Reece James. Alonso said James - who has missed long spells in recent seasons due to hamstring problems - had suffered a knee injury in training on Friday. Chelsea will face stiffer tests this season than Bournemouth who have not won any of their six games so far under new manager Marco Rose and were missing key players including England midfielder Alex Scott and strikers Eli Kroupi and Justin Kluivert. Alonso said Chelsea lost control of the game briefly when Bournemouth pulled a goal back through Evanilson to make it 3-1 in the 51st minute, but he took encouragement from the way they finished off the game with two goals in three minutes later on. "From today we take positives for the future," he said.

(Writing by William Schomberg, editing by Pritha Sarkar)

Oct 10 : French prodigy Paul Seixas rode solo to claim the first Monument victory of his career at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday, ahead of Spain's Enric Mas and Italy's Giulio Ciccone. The 20-year-old attacked 19 km from the finish in Como (Italy) to claim the title won by Tadej Pogacar for the last five years. The Slovenian missed the race after crashing at the Vuelta a Espana two months ago. Seixas won his first Monument — one of the five most prestigious one-day races in professional cycling — in his third appearance. He finished seventh in this race last year and second behind Pogacar at the last Liege–Bastogne–Liege. "It's crazy, it feels like a dream," Seixas said. "Everything went perfect. I had amazing legs, I had the feeling that today was a great day and I managed to make the difference at the moment I choose."

Seixas, who finished fourth in this year's Tour de France, pulled clear on the Civiglio climb with 19 km to go. Britain's Tom Pidcock and Ciccone were the only riders able to follow his wheel. The Frenchman dropped both rivals a few hundred metres later and rode alone over the final 18 km to become the youngest Monument winner since 1944 and youngest ever winner of the Giro di Lombardia. SEIXAS ENDS FRENCH WAIT The Decathlon–CMA CGM rider is the first Frenchman to win a Monument since Julian Alaphilippe at Milan–San Remo in 2019, and the first to triumph at the Giro di Lombardia since Thibaut Pinot in 2018. The victory came two weeks after a huge disappointment for Seixas at the World Championships, where he finished 15th after starting among the favourites. "After the championship, I moved on to other things; I trained hard to get here," Seixas said. "It’s incredible." The 239 km ride from Bergamo to Como began with a five-minute protest in the peloton to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles. After organisers completed the start countdown, the peloton remained stationary, before double Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel stepped forward to explain the riders' action. The protest came days after riders Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi were struck by a police motorcycle during Tre Valli Varesine. Britain's Finlay Tarling was killed in a collision with a vehicle during the Tour of Portugal in August.

Source: Reuters

AUGSBURG, Germany, Oct 10 : Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer scored after eight seconds of the game against visitors Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, but the German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 draw. Fellhauer benefited from a blunder by Bayern's Manuel Neuer as the keeper tried to clear but sent the ball to the Augsburg player who improved the record held jointly by Kevin Volland and Karim Bellarabi with goals after nine seconds. The Bavarians, whose only league defeat in their last 48 matches was by Augsburg in January, upped their game after the break, having an effort ruled offside in the 51st before Ismael Saibari bagged the equaliser four minutes later. It was another Neuer error that put Augsburg ahead again in the 64th minute, the 40-year-old punching Calvin Brackelmann's shot into the path of Rodrigo Ribeiro who only had to push the ball over the line. Bayern battled back once more, however, when Harry Kane, who hit the woodwork in the first half, cut the ball back for Nathaniel Brown to tap in the equaliser 10 minutes from time. Gnabry hit the post three minutes but Bayern had to settle for a point and second place on 11. Borussia Dortmund are top on 13 points.

Source: Reuters

MADRID, Oct 10 : The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half. The game was the first of this league season played at the Estadio de Vallecas, which was temporarily closed after an audit found serious safety issues. Rayo fans blame negligence by club owner Raul Martin Presa, who in turn accused regional authorities of deliberately targeting his club. The Sports Association of Rayo Vallecano fan group said in a statement after the suspension that their protest was "legitimate and democratic... necessary and peaceful."

It added that it was the "consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight". La Liga said in a statement on social media it "strongly condemned this type of behaviour, which endangers safety and makes the normal development of the competition impossible". A new date and time for the match will be announced shortly, LaLiga said. Athletic returned to Bilbao, saying on social media that LaLiga had communicated the game would not take place later on Saturday or on Sunday. Last season's Conference League finalists Rayo released a statement saying the club would seek to identify and discipline those responsible, adding that the forced postponement was part of a sustained campaign of disruption by the fan group.  The players, officials and supporters present were "victims of an attack on their rights and freedoms, committed by an organised group of intolerant individuals," said the statement. "UNSUSTAINABLE SITUATION" Rayo captain Oscar Valentin said on social media that "an unsustainable situation had reached its limit" and too little had been done to prevent things getting to this point. "It is necessary to listen to and understand the discontent of our fans. We need a way of bringing ALL parties closer together, always putting the common good first and, above all, the good of Rayo Vallecano," Valentin added. After Rayo's first three home games were moved to the stadium of second-tier Leganes, registering some of La Liga's lowest-ever attendance figures, home fans started chanting, jeering and whistling against Presa before kickoff on Saturday. By the 13th minute - when Rayo ultras usually chant the song "Presa leave already" - hundreds of fans launched paper planes and small rubber balls onto the pitch, prompting the referee to suspend play. A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects onto the field as staff hastily removed them. When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects onto the pitch and the referee abandoned the game. Anger at Presa's management has reached a peak in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas Stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season. In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

Source: Reuters

Oct 10 : Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday. The 41-year-old left the squad's base in Copenhagen before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.  Ronaldo, an unused substitute against Norway, accused Jesus of twice breaking his word regarding his role in the team. After Portugal's 2-1 win, Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player but left the door open for his return.

According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the FPF confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened against Ronaldo. "Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status," the federation was quoted as saying. FPF president Pedro Proenca said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved. "The Portuguese Football Federation and its president, in this spirit of tranquility, speaking with all parties, who have already publicly demonstrated their desire to have the captain back with us, there is an expressed wish from everyone," he was quoted as saying by A Bola. "This includes the federation, the FPF president, the national team coach, the captain and the players." Regarding Ronaldo's disciplinary process, Proenca added: "That will depend solely on the Disciplinary Committee, which is an autonomous body, and it will do its job." Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his teammates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

LONDON, Oct 10 : Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break. The competition returned under a cloud, with Manchester City found guilty by an independent commission of more than 100 breaches of the league's financial rules over nine years and their failure to co-operate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the decision. On the pitch, champions Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, behind City on goal difference before the Manchester club travel to Liverpool on Sunday.

Chelsea struck twice in the opening three minutes en route to a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, with Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro bagging two goals apiece, and are fifth on 10 points. Tottenham Hotspur struck in stoppage time to salvage a 1-1 draw at Manchester United as both sides' struggles continued. Brighton & Hove Albion climbed to third, two points off top spot, with a 2-0 win at Sunderland. Aston Villa and visiting Brentford drew 2-2, while Ipswich Town edged Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road with a last-gasp goal to leave the last-placed London side without a league victory this season. FRUSTRATING FIRST HALF Arsenal were looking to bounce back, having slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in the last game before the break but endured a frustrating first half as they struggled to create chances. Their play improved in the second period, but Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute when James Justin slammed home a clever pull-back from Gabriel Gudmundsson.  Riccardo Calafiori levelled for Arsenal seven minutes later, the Italian jumping to steer home Ben White's knock-down and, sensing his side could grab all three points, manager Mikel Arteta rang the changes.  He sent on Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres, and was rewarded when Guimaraes grabbed the winner with a brilliantly worked goal in the 70th minute, sending a low shot into the far corner of the net from the edge of the box. "It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said. "I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded." Leeds are sixth on nine points. UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score. Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva. Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick. Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022. At Old Trafford, Spurs were the better team but United punished their wastefulness in the 73rd minute when Matheus Cunha picked out Bryan Mbeumo in the box, and Mbeumo slotted home with United's second shot on target. Rodrigo Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a 78th-minute melee. But 10-man Spurs equalised in the 92nd minute when Dominic Solanke got away from Lisandro Martinez to nod Sandro Tonali's cross home for a well-deserved leveller that got them off the bottom of the table. They are 18th on three points, while United are 12th with six points. Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute. Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa. Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

Source: Reuters
